title: 📚👶Interview with Psychotherapist Win Schepps on Why Children Need to Know it’s Ok to Cry

sentences.en: All right, so this is Joel Blackstock with the Taproot Therapy Collective Podcast, and I'm here with Wyn Scheps, who has been a therapist for how long, Wyn?
sentences.zh: 好的，这位是来自 Taproot Therapy Collective 播客的 Joel Blackstock，我今天请到了 Wyn Scheps，Wyn，你做治疗师有多久了？

sentences.en: 57 years.
sentences.zh: 57年了。

sentences.en: 57 years.
And they're going to keep me until I learn to do it right.
sentences.zh: 他们打算一直留着我，直到我学会怎么把它做好为止。

sentences.en: And Wyn taught me Sunday school.
sentences.zh: Wyn 还教过我主日学。

sentences.en: My son is also named after him, and he was the first social worker and therapist that I encountered as a kid,
sentences.zh: 我儿子也是以他的名字命名的，他是我小时候接触到的第一位社会工作者和治疗师，

sentences.en: and I stayed consistently interested in what he did until I became a therapist myself.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我就一直对他所做的工作很感兴趣，直到我自己也成为了一名治疗师。

sentences.en: And so Wyn is 86 this year and still working?
sentences.zh: 所以 Wyn 今年 86 岁了，还在工作？

sentences.en: Four days a week.
sentences.zh: 每周工作四天。

sentences.en: You've got to learn to save so you can retire.
sentences.zh: 你得学会存钱，这样才能退休。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I want to get rich life to get up and retire.
sentences.zh: 我想发财，然后退休。

sentences.en: Wyn loves it a lot.
sentences.zh: Wyn 非常热爱这份工作。

sentences.en: Yes, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实很热爱。

sentences.en: You told me years ago, I don't have to work anymore.
sentences.zh: 你多年前曾告诉我，我不需要再工作了。

sentences.en: I just love working so damn much.
sentences.zh: 但我就是太热爱这份工作了。

sentences.en: I love what I do.
sentences.zh: 我热爱我所做的一切。

sentences.en: So Wyn has a children's book that we'll get to at the end that he wrote, but I think like a lot of therapists, there's kind of a lot of pain in his story,
sentences.zh: Wyn 写了一本儿童读物，我们最后会提到它。但我觉得像许多治疗师一样，他的故事里也藏着不少痛苦，

sentences.en: and his story has always been really compelling to me.
sentences.zh: 而他的故事一直以来都让我深感触动。

sentences.en: So if you want to, we can just kind of start at the beginning of your life and go through your career because you've seen a ton of history, too.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你愿意的话，我们可以从你生命的开端讲起，回顾一下你的职业生涯，因为你也见证了太多的历史。

sentences.en: I mean, like the profession, you were trained psychoanalytically.
sentences.zh: 我是说，就这个行业而言，你接受过精神分析方面的训练。

sentences.en: You know, you're like doing therapy in the beginning and then you...
sentences.zh: 你知道，你刚开始做治疗的时候，然后你……

sentences.en: Psychoanalytically, no.
sentences.zh: 精神分析？没有。

sentences.en: I have a master's from NYU in psychiatric social work.
sentences.zh: 我拥有纽约大学精神病学社会工作的硕士学位。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But you were in psychoanalysis and the supervisor...
sentences.zh: 但你当时在接受精神分析，而且督导……

sentences.en: I was in psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 我当时在接受心理治疗。

sentences.en: I've never been in psychoanalysis.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有接受过精神分析。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But there was a lot more Freudian stuff in the water, you know, pre-1980.
sentences.zh: 但在 1980 年之前，弗洛伊德的思想确实影响深远，你知道的。

sentences.en: The cognitive revolution comes in and CBT becomes real big.
sentences.zh: 后来认知革命到来，CBT（认知行为疗法）变得非常流行。

sentences.en: But you've just seen a ton of history.
sentences.zh: 但你确实见证了太多的历史。

sentences.en: You've seen the profession change.
sentences.zh: 你见证了这个行业的变迁。

sentences.en: Yes, I have.
sentences.zh: 是的，我见证了。

sentences.en: So, I guess, where do you want to start?
sentences.zh: 那么，我想，你想从哪里开始讲起呢？

sentences.en: I mean, can you feel comfortable telling us a little bit about the early, the beginning of your life?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能自在地跟我们聊聊你早年，也就是你生命的开端吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: I was born and raised in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我在俄亥俄州出生长大。

sentences.en: I'm the second of two children.
sentences.zh: 我是两个孩子中的老二。

sentences.en: I have an older brother, four or five years older than me.
sentences.zh: 我有一个哥哥，比我大四五岁。

sentences.en: I pretty much always felt he was more okay than I was.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得他比我更“正常”一些。

sentences.en: Maybe a part of that comes from the theory that the first child is more like the more dominant parent and the second child is more like the other parent.
sentences.zh: 也许部分原因源于一种理论，即第一个孩子更像性格强势的父母，而第二个孩子更像另一方父母。

sentences.en: I was always more like my mother and my older brother was more like dad.
sentences.zh: 我总是更像我母亲，而我哥哥更像我父亲。

sentences.en: I didn't really know my dad because he was training to go overseas as a part of World War II.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太了解我父亲，因为他在二战期间正在接受海外派驻训练。

sentences.en: In fact, his plane crashed in Presquick, Scotland, when he was flying over to lead an armored infantry unit under General Patton shortly after D-Day.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在诺曼底登陆后不久，在飞往巴顿将军麾下指挥一支装甲步兵部队的途中，飞机在苏格兰的普雷斯威克坠毁了。

sentences.en: I was seven or eight years old.
sentences.zh: 那时我才七八岁。

sentences.en: I remember faking crying when the telegram came that the dad had died because everyone else was crying.
sentences.zh: 我记得当父亲去世的电报传来时，我假装在哭，因为其他人都在哭。

sentences.en: I didn't really know the man, so I thought in order to be a part of the family, I should probably cry too.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不了解那个人，所以我认为为了融入这个家庭，我也应该哭。

sentences.en: The family moved to Hollywood because I had taken tap dancing for about four or five years, and I found out later in my therapy that I may have been living my mother's script
sentences.zh: 后来全家搬到了好莱坞，因为我学了四五年的踢踏舞，后来我在治疗中发现，我可能一直在按照母亲的剧本生活，

sentences.en: because she had been a frustrated actress.
sentences.zh: 因为她曾是一位不得志的演员。

sentences.en: Please feel free to interrupt at any point in order to expand, y'all.
sentences.zh: 大家随时可以打断我进行补充。

sentences.en: I'm proud to say that I even tried out for the part of the only white boy tap dancer in the movie Singing in the Rain, but I wasn't cute enough or I didn't dance good enough.
sentences.zh: 我很自豪地说，我甚至参加过电影《雨中曲》里那个唯一的白人小男孩踢踏舞者的试镜，但我当时不够可爱，或者舞跳得不够好。

sentences.en: So that was about the point my mother developed breast cancer, which she intestinalized.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我母亲患上了乳腺癌，她把它内化了。

sentences.en: In the early 40s, the only treatment for breast cancer was mustard gas.
sentences.zh: 在 40 年代初期，治疗乳腺癌的唯一方法是芥子气。

sentences.en: She received mustard gas treatment, but she died when I was 11.
sentences.zh: 她接受了芥子气治疗，但在我 11 岁时去世了。

sentences.en: I remember being very critical of myself when I was standing outside of mom's room because I thought I needed to tell her goodbye, but I couldn't.
sentences.zh: 我记得站在母亲房间外时，我对自己非常苛刻，因为我觉得我需要跟她告别，但我做不到。

sentences.en: And as a therapist, I've learned I couldn't say goodbye because that would have confirmed she was dying.
sentences.zh: 作为一名治疗师，我后来明白我无法告别，因为那意味着确认她真的要死了。

sentences.en: And as an 11-year-old, I could not accept she was dying.
sentences.zh: 而作为一个 11 岁的孩子，我无法接受她即将离世的事实。

sentences.en: She died when I was 11.
sentences.zh: 她在我 11 岁时去世了。

sentences.en: I began to stutter at that point, trying too hard to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 从那时起我开始结巴，因为我太想表现得完美了。

sentences.en: I'm not sure why, except I do feel the stuttering is trying to avoid stuttering.
sentences.zh: 我不确定原因，但我确实觉得结巴本身就是一种试图避免结巴的努力。

sentences.en: And in my own talking therapy, I've had, I've probably had five or six different therapists.
sentences.zh: 在我自己的谈话治疗中，我大概找过五六位不同的治疗师。

sentences.en: I've probably had 500 to 1,000 hours of therapy to get me to my present level of security.
sentences.zh: 我可能接受了 500 到 1000 小时的治疗，才达到了现在这种安全感水平。

sentences.en: I moved in with my aunt and uncle.
sentences.zh: 我搬去和姑姑姑父住在一起。

sentences.en: My brother stayed in Hollywood to finish high school.
sentences.zh: 我哥哥留在好莱坞读完了高中。

sentences.en: I was raised by another West Point graduate.
sentences.zh: 我是由另一位西点军校毕业生抚养长大的。

sentences.en: My father was a West Point graduate.
sentences.zh: 我父亲也是西点军校毕业生。

sentences.en: My brother moved into a different home when we were 11.
sentences.zh: 我们 11 岁时，哥哥搬到了另一个家庭。

sentences.en: And so I really, in essence, lost my entire nuclear family.
sentences.zh: 所以，本质上，我失去了整个核心家庭。

sentences.en: I thought I should become perfect for fear my aunt and uncle might kick me out.
sentences.zh: 我以为我必须变得完美，因为害怕姑姑姑父会把我赶出去。

sentences.en: So when we went to my mother's funeral, my aunt told me not to cry.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们去参加母亲的葬礼时，姑姑告诉我不要哭。

sentences.en: Your mom wouldn't want you to.
sentences.zh: 你妈妈不会希望你哭的。

sentences.en: Thus, the book, 80 years later.
sentences.zh: 于是，就有了这本书，80 年后。

sentences.en: Yeah, you've told me long before the book existed, 20 years before the book existed, one had always told me that one of his biggest goals in life was to write a children's book,
sentences.zh: 是的，早在书出版之前，甚至在书构思的 20 年前，Wyn 就一直告诉我，他人生最大的目标之一就是写一本儿童读物，

sentences.en: convincing children that it was okay to cry.
sentences.zh: 去告诉孩子们哭泣是没关系的。

sentences.en: So it's been a long time coming to write your book.
sentences.zh: 所以这本书酝酿了很久。

sentences.en: A hell of a long time, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实是太久了，是的。

sentences.en: I was raised by my aunt and uncle.
sentences.zh: 我是由姑姑姑父抚养长大的。

sentences.en: I was never ordered to go to West Point.
sentences.zh: 他们从未强迫我一定要去西点军校。

sentences.en: But I was told, since we didn't have any money, West Point is free.
sentences.zh: 但他们告诉我，因为我们没钱，西点军校是免费的。

sentences.en: I could get a very fine education.
sentences.zh: 我可以接受非常好的教育。

sentences.en: West Point being the military army academy, if anyone's underage.
sentences.zh: 如果有人未成年，西点军校就是陆军军官学校。

sentences.en: The United States Military Academy of West Point in New York.
sentences.zh: 位于纽约的美国西点陆军军官学校。

sentences.en: But West Point's army, right?
sentences.zh: 但西点是陆军的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What's the Navy in the Annapolis?
sentences.zh: 那安纳波利斯的海军学校呢？

sentences.en: The Navy is Annapolis.
sentences.zh: 海军是安纳波利斯。

sentences.en: And then what's the, is it the Air Force?
sentences.zh: 那还有什么，是空军吗？

sentences.en: The Air Force is in Colorado Springs, Colorado.
sentences.zh: 空军在科罗拉多州的科罗拉多斯普林斯。

sentences.en: It's the Air Force Academy.
sentences.zh: 那是空军学院。

sentences.en: Why army as opposed to another branch?
sentences.zh: 为什么选择陆军而不是其他军种？

sentences.en: Because my father, uncle, and brother had all gone to West Point.
sentences.zh: 因为我父亲、叔叔和哥哥都去过西点军校。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And I was living my family script.
sentences.zh: 我当时是在按照家庭剧本生活。

sentences.en: Script, S-C-R-I-P-T.
sentences.zh: 剧本，S-C-R-I-P-T。

sentences.en: My family script.
sentences.zh: 我的家庭剧本。

sentences.en: I didn't cry.
sentences.zh: 我不哭。

sentences.en: I didn't get angry.
sentences.zh: 我不生气。

sentences.en: I did have the courage many years later to tell my uncle that when I was angry, I bore holes in his floor.
sentences.zh: 多年后，我终于有勇气告诉叔叔，当我生气时，我会在他的地板上钻洞。

sentences.en: Because my talking therapy that I did helped me know it's okay to feel what you feel.
sentences.zh: 因为我所做的谈话治疗帮助我明白，感受自己的情绪是没关系的。

sentences.en: In fact, one of the theories that I've held to, Joel, is that if you're not psychotic or have a brain tumor, you can't feel anything wrong.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我一直坚持的一个理论是，Joel，如果你没有精神病或脑肿瘤，你就不可能产生错误的感受。

sentences.en: So, therapy has really helped me.
sentences.zh: 所以，治疗真的帮了我很多。

sentences.en: And being a therapist, I feel a lot of people I know, if not most therapists, are people who have had therapy and people who are trying to be helpful to others as a way of being
sentences.zh: 作为一名治疗师，我觉得我认识的很多人，如果不是大多数治疗师的话，都是接受过治疗的人，他们试图帮助他人，以此作为帮助自己的一种方式。

sentences.en: helpful to themselves.
sentences.zh: 帮助自己。

sentences.en: So, having a lot of pressure, you go to West Point, a free education.
sentences.zh: 所以，在巨大的压力下，你去了西点军校，接受免费教育。

sentences.en: In fact, you get paid for going to the academy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，去军校还有工资拿。

sentences.en: I went to West Point.
sentences.zh: 我去了西点军校。

sentences.en: I graduated in 1959.
sentences.zh: 我 1959 年毕业。

sentences.en: I did infantry airborne school because my brother, who was a West Boiler also, told me that I should.
sentences.zh: 我参加了步兵空降学校，因为我哥哥，他也是西点毕业的，告诉我我应该去。

sentences.en: Should is a word that I believe comes from the critical parent ego state, not the nurturing parent ego state, by the way, for the record.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，记录在案，“应该”这个词我认为来自批判型父母自我状态，而不是滋养型父母自我状态。

sentences.en: So, I served my three years.
sentences.zh: 所以，我服役了三年。

sentences.en: I called my uncle, Colonel McGee, who was in charge of the military part of President Roosevelt's
sentences.zh: 我给我的叔叔 McGee 上校打了电话，他曾负责罗斯福总统葬礼的军事部分，

sentences.en: funeral, and told him I was going to resign my commission and go into psychiatric social work.
sentences.zh: 告诉他我要辞去军职，去从事精神病学社会工作。

sentences.en: My uncle's words, quote, you'll be poor.
sentences.zh: 我叔叔的话，引用一下：“你会变穷的。”

sentences.en: You'll be poor, Winnie.
sentences.zh: “你会变穷的，Winnie。”

sentences.en: All you got to do is serve 13 more years.
sentences.zh: “你只需要再服役 13 年就行了。”

sentences.en: And I had found the courage in my own therapy to say, Judson, this feels like it's terribly important for me to do, to help others and the process of myself.
sentences.zh: 我在自己的治疗中找到了勇气说：“Judson，我觉得做这件事对我来说非常重要，为了帮助他人，也为了我自己。”

sentences.en: But Winnie, you'll be poor.
sentences.zh: “但是 Winnie，你会变穷的。”

sentences.en: So, I called my brother, who had also known to West Point, the audience may remember, and he said, go for it.
sentences.zh: 于是，我给哥哥打了电话，他也去过西点军校，观众可能还记得，他说：“去吧，放手去做。”

sentences.en: I could try saying that.
sentences.zh: 我可以试着说那句话。

sentences.en: And if my first book does well, I'm going to write another book called, go for it, and dedicate it to my older brother.
sentences.zh: 如果我的第一本书卖得好，我就要写第二本书，书名就叫《放手去做》，并把它献给我的哥哥。

sentences.en: So, I did go for it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我真的放手去做了。

sentences.en: I got out of the military.
sentences.zh: 我退伍了。

sentences.en: I called Adelphi and said, I'm ready to enter graduate school.
sentences.zh: 我给 Adelphi 打电话说，我准备好进入研究生院了。

sentences.en: And they said, it don't work that way, Sheps.
sentences.zh: 他们说：“事情不是那样运作的，Sheps。”

sentences.en: You have to give us a transcript, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: “你得给我们提供成绩单，等等等等。”

sentences.en: So, I got a job at a residential treatment center for emotionally disturbed Jewish children and began to learn about the field of being a therapist and as a way of getting to know
sentences.zh: 于是，我在一家针对情绪障碍犹太儿童的寄宿治疗中心找了份工作，开始了解治疗师这个领域，这也成了我了解父亲信仰的一种方式，因为他曾是犹太人。

sentences.en: my father's faith because he had been Jewish.
sentences.zh: 他曾是犹太人。

sentences.en: I did enter NYU, even though Columbia turned me down because my grades at West Point were just terrible.
sentences.zh: 我确实进入了纽约大学，尽管哥伦比亚大学拒绝了我，因为我在西点军校的成绩实在太差了。

sentences.en: And I took a test to prove I was not an idiot.
sentences.zh: 我参加了一场考试来证明我不是个白痴。

sentences.en: I got into NYU.
sentences.zh: 我考进了纽约大学。

sentences.en: I got a master's in psychiatric social work in 1965, during which time I had been coming
sentences.zh: 我在 1965 年获得了精神病学社会工作硕士学位，在此期间，我一直去伯明翰探望我的一位陆军朋友，他把我介绍给了一位叫 Michael Kay 的女士。

sentences.en: to Birmingham to visit an Army friend of mine, and he had introduced me to a lady named Michael
sentences.zh: 去伯明翰探望我的一位军中好友，他把我介绍给了一位名叫迈克尔的女士

sentences.en: Kay.
sentences.zh: Kay。

sentences.en: And that part of my life became history because I did come back to Birmingham to work for the
sentences.zh: 我生命中的那一部分成了历史，因为我确实回到了伯明翰，在精神病学系工作，我们又约会了几次。

sentences.en: Department of Psychiatry, and we dated some more.
sentences.zh: 在我的治疗中，我从第一位精神科医生、第一位咨询师那里获得了信念，那就是我原本的样子就是可爱的，包括我所有的感受。

sentences.en: And I found the belief in my own therapy, first psychiatrist, first counselor I saw, that I was lovable as I was to include all my feelings.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有精神病或脑肿瘤，你就不可能产生错误的感受。

sentences.en: If you're not psychotic or don't have a brain tumor, you can't feel anything wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们拥有了 47 年美满的婚姻。

sentences.en: So, we had a wonderful 47-year marriage.
sentences.zh: 我们结婚后不久，她患上了卵巢癌，差点去世，但她被治愈了。

sentences.en: She developed cancer in the ovaries shortly after we got married and almost died, but she got cured.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们领养了孩子，除了那些我真想杀了他们的罕见时刻——世界上没有任何陪审团会把我关进监狱——

sentences.en: So, we have adopted children, and other than those rare times, I could have killed them, and no jury in the world would have put me in jail.
sentences.zh: 我什么都不会改变。

sentences.en: I wouldn't change a thing.
sentences.zh: Warren 和 Scott 是我生命中的挚爱，自从我大约 10 年前不幸因癌症失去她之后。

sentences.en: Warren Scott are the loves of my life, since I lost my life about 10 years ago to, unfortunately, cancer.
sentences.zh: 我开展了心理治疗业务。

sentences.en: I developed a practice in psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，我见过 5 到 10 位不同的治疗师，他们帮助我认识到我是好的，我的感受也是好的，我开始在脑海中写一本书。

sentences.en: I've seen, as I said earlier, 5 to 10 different therapists who have helped me know that I am okay, my feelings are okay, and I started writing a book in my head.
sentences.zh: “哭泣可以吗？”因为我的姑姑……

sentences.en: Is it okay to cry because of my aunt...
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你。

sentences.en: God bless you.
sentences.zh: 因为我姑姑在葬礼上告诉我，我妈妈不会希望我哭。

sentences.en: Because of my aunt telling me my mom wouldn't want me to cry at the funeral.
sentences.zh: 所以，我开始在脑海中写书，我又遇见了一位非常亲密的朋友，那是我遇见妻子那个夏天认识的，当时我们还在约会，她基本上告诉我，如果我不出版这本书，我就太没种了，这听起来对她来说很棒。

sentences.en: So, I began writing a book in my head, and I remet a very dear friend that I had met the summer that I met my wife while we were still dating, who basically told me I didn't have
sentences.zh: 没有

sentences.en: any guts if I didn't publish this book that has sounded wonderful for her.
sentences.zh: 任何胆量

sentences.en: And I thought about what she said, and I thought, that's right, and the book might really help
sentences.zh: 我思考了她的话，心想，说得对，这本书或许真的能帮到

sentences.en: a lot of people, because family scripts tend to teach boys don't get sad and girls don't cry.
sentences.zh: 很多人，因为家庭剧本往往教导男孩不要难过，女孩不要哭泣。

sentences.en: That's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: If you're now psychotic or don't have a brain tumor, you can't feel anything wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有精神病，也没有脑肿瘤，你就不可能感觉不到哪里不对劲。

sentences.en: And in my own personal therapy with other therapists, and my own practice as a psychotherapist, I learned that's a good thinking that I could share with the world in a book.
sentences.zh: 在我自己与其他治疗师的个人治疗中，以及我作为心理治疗师的实践中，我意识到这是一个可以写进书里与世界分享的好想法。

sentences.en: So, the book became, Is It Okay to Cry, dedicated to my friend, Pugs Douglas.
sentences.zh: 于是，这本书就成了《哭泣可以吗？》，并献给我的朋友帕格斯·道格拉斯（Pugs Douglas）。

sentences.en: I couldn't find a publisher who wanted to publish it, so I paid to have it published, and I'm very proud to say that I do feel that that dream of mine has been fulfilled.
sentences.zh: 我找不到愿意出版它的出版商，所以我自费出版了，我很自豪地说，我觉得我的那个梦想已经实现了。

sentences.en: So, you've been in therapy a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你接受治疗已经很长时间了。

sentences.en: I mean, are the styles of therapy you're in, are they similar?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你所接受的治疗风格，它们相似吗？

sentences.en: Do you notice, like, a change in things over time, you know, having been a patient and a provider, you know, for how many years?
sentences.zh: 你有没有注意到，随着时间的推移，事情发生了变化，毕竟你既当过病人，也当过提供者，这么多年了？

sentences.en: 57 years.
sentences.zh: 57年了。

sentences.en: Yes, I've learned there are other styles, but the other styles are not right for me.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道还有其他风格，但其他风格不适合我。

sentences.en: Or I'm an old farmer who doesn't want to change, I'm not sure, Joel.
sentences.zh: 又或者我是一个不想改变的老农夫，我不确定，乔尔。

sentences.en: So, you were a cognitive behavioral therapist?
sentences.zh: 所以，你以前是认知行为治疗师？

sentences.en: I do some CBT, I do some gestalt work, I do some psychodrama, I like role play, but I
sentences.zh: 我做一些CBT（认知行为疗法），做一些格式塔疗法，做一些心理剧，我喜欢角色扮演，但我

sentences.en: mainly like talking, because my talking therapy has helped me learn that when I lost everybody, I became what anyone else wanted me to be.
sentences.zh: 主要还是喜欢谈话，因为我的谈话疗法帮助我认识到，当我失去所有人时，我变成了别人想要我成为的样子。

sentences.en: I lost me.
sentences.zh: 我迷失了自我。

sentences.en: And in the last 20, 25 years, I have reclaimed me, and that feels absolutely wonderful.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20到25年里，我找回了自我，那种感觉真是太美妙了。

sentences.en: So, I've continued doing talking work.
sentences.zh: 所以，我继续从事谈话疗法的工作。

sentences.en: I don't do EMDr.
sentences.zh: 我不做EMDR（眼动脱敏再加工）。

sentences.en: I don't do brain spotting.
sentences.zh: 我不做大脑点位疗法（Brainspotting）。

sentences.en: You obviously do that wonderfully, but those things are not right for me to do as an untrained person.
sentences.zh: 你显然做得非常出色，但作为一名未经培训的人，做这些并不适合我。

sentences.en: Sure, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: And when, there's also like, it seems like there's always been a through line of like a lot of the humanitarian, like Virginia Satir type stuff, and what you've described
sentences.zh: 而且，似乎一直有一条主线，比如很多像弗吉尼亚·萨提亚（Virginia Satir）那样的仁爱理念，以及你所描述的

sentences.en: your conceptualizations.
sentences.zh: 你的概念化方式。

sentences.en: Did you know Satir, or go train with her?
sentences.zh: 你认识萨提亚，或者跟她一起训练过吗？

sentences.en: I once entertained her, as a matter of fact, in my home.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我曾经在家里招待过她。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: I did not know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Lovely, lovely lady.
sentences.zh: 可爱，非常可爱的女士。

sentences.en: I do a lot of grief work, because I've had a lot of grief in my own life, and I do cry with clients when I feel like crying.
sentences.zh: 我做很多悲伤辅导，因为我自己的生活中经历过很多悲伤，当我想哭的时候，我会和来访者一起哭。

sentences.en: She was a wonderful lady.
sentences.zh: 她是一位了不起的女士。

sentences.en: She did wonderful, wonderful grief work.
sentences.zh: 她做了非常、非常棒的悲伤辅导工作。

sentences.en: She did wonderful book work.
sentences.zh: 她做了很棒的书籍工作。

sentences.en: Rest her soul.
sentences.zh: 愿她安息。

sentences.en: So, you're integrated then, and there's a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，你是综合型的，而且有很多内容。

sentences.en: I know about the way that you talk about cases, because I've heard about it since Sunday school.
sentences.zh: 我知道你谈论案例的方式，因为我从主日学起就听说了。

sentences.en: You'd even bring cases in when I was in sixth grade, sometimes.
sentences.zh: 甚至在我六年级的时候，你有时也会带案例进来。

sentences.en: Without mentioning names.
sentences.zh: 不提名字。

sentences.en: Without mentioning names, of course, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，不提名字，是的。

sentences.en: No identifiable information.
sentences.zh: 没有可识别的信息。

sentences.en: So, I have a sense of how you think.
sentences.zh: 所以我对你的思维方式有一定了解。

sentences.en: I'm just curious, you know, how you got there, what you're putting together.
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇，你是怎么达到这一点的，你是如何整合这些东西的。

sentences.en: And that makes sense that there's some gestalt from CBT, and the kind of humanism, human potential, Virginia Satir stuff.
sentences.zh: 把CBT的格式塔，以及那种人文主义、人类潜能、弗吉尼亚·萨提亚的东西结合起来，这很有道理。

sentences.en: But it does seem like there is some more psychoanalytic concepts come up when you're talking than with most providers that I talk to.
sentences.zh: 但比起我交谈过的大多数提供者，当你说话时，似乎确实出现了更多精神分析的概念。

sentences.en: I mean, is that just more in the water in the 60s?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那只是60年代的普遍风气吗？

sentences.en: Do you think everybody got a little bit of that?
sentences.zh: 你认为每个人都受了点影响吗？

sentences.en: More in the water, yeah.
sentences.zh: 普遍风气，是的。

sentences.en: I learned that at NYU, humans are the only animal that spent 18 years at home and the next 40 getting over it.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约大学学到，人类是唯一一种在家待18年，然后花40年去克服它的动物。

sentences.en: Men tend to live through their male children.
sentences.zh: 男人往往通过他们的儿子来生活。

sentences.en: Men tend to have the highest expectation for their oldest son.
sentences.zh: 男人往往对长子抱有最高的期望。

sentences.en: And I'm very pleased to say that I and my son are doing so much better, even kissing, when
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地说，我和我儿子现在相处得好多了，甚至会亲吻，当

sentences.en: I learned to lower my expectations for him.
sentences.zh: 我学会降低对他的期望时。

sentences.en: I'm okay because I'm okay, not because I have a perfect son.
sentences.zh: 我很好，因为我就是我，而不是因为我有一个完美的儿子。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that is one of the biggest things that gets the unlived life of the parent out
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是让父母未竟的人生摆脱干扰的最大因素之一

sentences.en: of the way, as if you can just not make your kids be an extension of your ego and just let them be who they are supposed to be, because who they are supposed to be is pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 只要你不让孩子成为你自我的延伸，让他们成为他们本该成为的样子，因为他们本该成为的样子就很酷。

sentences.en: One of the other things I learned, and you may remember seeing this in Walmart, people don't remember what you did for them.
sentences.zh: 我学到的另一件事，你可能记得在沃尔玛见过这个，人们不记得你为他们做了什么。

sentences.en: People remember how you made them feel.
sentences.zh: 人们记得你让他们感觉如何。

sentences.en: And I've always been more sensitive than my older brother because he was more like dad and I was more like mom.
sentences.zh: 我一直比我哥哥更敏感，因为他更像爸爸，而我更像妈妈。

sentences.en: So I try to practice sensitivity with my clients and help them know that they can pretty much be anything they want to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我尝试对我的来访者实践这种敏感性，帮助他们知道他们几乎可以成为他们想成为的任何人。

sentences.en: So I got a job as a psychiatric social worker at UAB right out of school, and I called you to tell you about it.
sentences.zh: 我刚毕业就在阿拉巴马大学伯明翰分校（UAB）找到了一份精神科社会工作者的工作，我打电话告诉你这个消息。

sentences.en: And you said, oh, I got a job at UAB as a psychiatric social worker in what, 1962?
sentences.zh: 你说，哦，我在1962年就在UAB找到了一份精神科社会工作者的工作，是吗？

sentences.en: What was it?
sentences.zh: 那是哪一年？

sentences.en: And you said you were making $6,000 was the...
sentences.zh: 你说你当时挣6000美元，那是……

sentences.en: $6,000, a loaf of bread costs $5,000.
sentences.zh: 6000美元，一条面包都要5000美元。

sentences.en: Well, it does now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在是这样。

sentences.en: And then you said once you had your first supervision session, it was interrupted.
sentences.zh: 然后你说你第一次督导会议就被打断了。

sentences.en: Can you tell that story?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲那个故事吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I can.
sentences.zh: 是的，我可以。

sentences.en: It was 19...
I forget the year.
sentences.zh: 我忘了年份了。

sentences.en: I was meeting with my supervisor while I was doing the field placement with retarded adults.
sentences.zh: 我在做智障成人的实地实习时，正在和我的督导会面。

sentences.en: At least that was the word that was used in those days, retarded.
sentences.zh: 至少那是当时使用的词，智障。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think they're trying to retire that now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想他们现在正试图淘汰这个词。

sentences.en: They wanted to have...
sentences.zh: 他们想有……

sentences.en: Now we say downs and other things like that.
sentences.zh: 现在我们说唐氏综合症和其他类似的东西。

sentences.en: And someone came to the door, and Murray Eskowitz, my supervisor, said, they know better than to interrupt me when I'm in supervision.
sentences.zh: 有人敲门，我的督导默里·埃斯科维茨（Murray Eskowitz）说，他们应该知道在我督导时不要打扰我。

sentences.en: This better be important.
sentences.zh: 最好是有什么重要的事情。

sentences.en: And someone came to the door and said, President Kennedy has been shot.
sentences.zh: 有人走到门口说，肯尼迪总统被枪杀了。

sentences.en: Well, it's a ton of history.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一段沉重的历史。

sentences.en: So supervision ended.
sentences.zh: 所以督导结束了。

sentences.en: But the most powerful thing that came out of that gift, since Kennedy had been like a father figure to me, was that night I had a dream, not a nightmare, that my father was
sentences.zh: 但那份礼物带来的最强大的东西是，因为肯尼迪对我来说就像父亲一样，那天晚上我做了一个梦，不是噩梦，梦见我父亲

sentences.en: in a casket in the White House and sat up to tell me goodbye.
sentences.zh: 躺在白宫的棺材里，坐起来跟我告别。

sentences.en: Because I'd never really said goodbye to my father, feeling tears in my voice now.
sentences.zh: 因为我从未真正向我父亲告别，现在我的声音里充满了泪水。

sentences.en: Looking at my book, is it okay to cry?
sentences.zh: 看着我的书，《哭泣可以吗？》

sentences.en: Yes, it's okay to cry.
sentences.zh: 是的，哭泣是可以的。

sentences.en: And so I had a chance to tell him goodbye.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个机会向他告别。

sentences.en: And as a matter of fact, me and my son will be going to New York, and I'll be taking flowers to my parents' grave in about a month.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我和我儿子大约一个月后要去纽约，我会去给我父母的坟墓献花。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And you had told me a story about one time, too, after a lot of therapy, you know, you felt resolved.
sentences.zh: 你也曾告诉过我一个故事，在经过大量治疗后，你知道，你感到释然了。

sentences.en: And somebody, maybe it was Sandy, said that they said, why don't you try this gestalt chair work, and why don't you talk to mom in this chair?
sentences.zh: 有人，也许是桑迪，说他们建议，为什么不试试这个格式塔椅疗法，为什么不跟椅子上的妈妈谈谈？

sentences.en: Can you tell that story?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲那个故事吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I can.
sentences.zh: 是的，我可以。

sentences.en: Sandy being Sandy Ash, one of my dearest friends in the world, who I'm now practicing with also.
sentences.zh: 桑迪就是桑迪·阿什（Sandy Ash），我世界上最亲爱的朋友之一，我现在也和她一起执业。

sentences.en: And I had a dear friend, Sue Brownell, who asked me if I'd be willing to meet my deceased mother and talk with her.
sentences.zh: 我有一位亲爱的朋友，苏·布朗内尔（Sue Brownell），她问我是否愿意去见我已故的母亲并与她交谈。

sentences.en: And I said, yes.
sentences.zh: 我说，愿意。

sentences.en: And she said, who would you like to play your mother?
sentences.zh: 她说，你想让谁扮演你的母亲？

sentences.en: And I said, you.
sentences.zh: 我说，你。

sentences.en: And we pulled two chairs to the middle of the room, and she looked at me with all the love
sentences.zh: 我们把两把椅子拉到房间中间，她带着所有的爱看着我，

sentences.en: Sue always felt as I felt for her, and said, hey, son.
sentences.zh: 苏一直感受到的，正如我感受到她的一样，她说，嘿，儿子。

sentences.en: And before I could get in touch with the proper way to respond, I got in touch with who I was.
sentences.zh: 在我能找到合适的应对方式之前，我先触碰到了真实的自我。

sentences.en: And before I became aware of it, Joel, my primal scream screamed, why did you leave me?
sentences.zh: 在我意识到之前，乔尔，我原始的尖叫声喊道，你为什么要离开我？

sentences.en: And I cried for like 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我哭了大约15分钟。

sentences.en: And there was something that I needed to say.
sentences.zh: 有些话是我需要说的。

sentences.en: And we did work through that it wasn't her fault she had died.
sentences.zh: 我们确实解决了她去世并不是她的错这个问题。

sentences.en: And that she loved me, and that I was okay.
sentences.zh: 她爱我，我很好。

sentences.en: So I like two-chair work, I like gestalt work, I like psychodromal work.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢双椅疗法，我喜欢格式塔疗法，我喜欢心理剧疗法。

sentences.en: But that was a very powerful experience that helped me know it's okay to feel what you feel.
sentences.zh: 但那是一次非常强大的体验，它帮助我知道，感受你的感受是可以的。

sentences.en: I got angry, and I cried.
sentences.zh: 我生气了，我哭了。

sentences.en: I think sometimes we forget what we feel because we know too much to let ourselves feel it.
sentences.zh: 我想有时我们忘记了我们的感受，因为我们知道得太多，以至于不让自己去感受它。

sentences.en: You know, we do all this analysis.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们做了所有的分析。

sentences.en: Well said, you ever thought I'd be in a psychotherapist?
sentences.zh: 说得好，你有没有想过我会成为一名心理治疗师？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm working on it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我正在努力。

sentences.en: But, you know, we know all this stuff, and we've analyzed our past, and we know all these patterns, and we have all this cognitive intellectual work.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们知道所有这些东西，我们分析了我们的过去，我们知道所有这些模式，我们有所有这些认知上的智力工作。

sentences.en: But we forget to just let go and feel what is beneath the surface and to get it out.
sentences.zh: 但我们忘记了去放手，去感受表面之下的东西，并把它释放出来。

sentences.en: And I think you were good at that, you know, using talk therapy to build a gateway to the felt experience, which is important.
sentences.zh: 我认为你很擅长这一点，你知道，利用谈话疗法建立通往感官体验的门户，这很重要。

sentences.en: I mean, I would say it's the point.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我会说这就是重点。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: One of the things that's always struck me about you, I'm remembering, like, when we were in, what do they call it,
sentences.zh: 有一件事一直让我印象深刻，我记得，比如，当我们参加，他们称之为什么，

sentences.en: grand rounds or sports rounds at UAB, there's an auditorium of several thousand people.
sentences.zh: UAB的教学查房或运动查房，那里有一个容纳几千人的礼堂。

sentences.en: And it's not really something that's supposed to be call and response.
sentences.zh: 那并不是那种应该有互动回应的场合。

sentences.en: And, like, your hand would go up, and you would scream over the whole auditorium, and the doctor would be like, oh, I guess we have a question.
sentences.zh: 然后，你的手会举起来，你会对着整个礼堂大喊，医生会说，哦，我想我们有一个问题。

sentences.en: You know, is that you refuse to not speak when you feel something.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那就是你拒绝在有感觉时保持沉默。

sentences.en: And I think that's really powerful.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的很强大。

sentences.en: You know, like, there's never a time where you feel insecure saying anything, you know, almost to a compulsion.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从来没有什么时候你会觉得说出任何话是不安全的，几乎到了强迫的地步。

sentences.en: And I wonder, you know, how much of that comes from being a kid that wasn't allowed to say what they felt or didn't even maybe know what you felt because there was no room for it.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，这在多大程度上源于你小时候不被允许说出自己的感受，或者甚至可能根本不知道自己的感受，因为没有空间去表达。

sentences.en: It's something you just refuse to be, you know, turned off now.
sentences.zh: 这是你现在拒绝被关闭的东西。

sentences.en: I can remember when my older brother came back from West Point.
sentences.zh: 我记得我哥哥从西点军校回来的时候。

sentences.en: I was having a problem talking on the phone, and I wasn't able to say hello.
sentences.zh: 我在打电话时遇到了问题，我无法说出你好。

sentences.en: And it came out for the audience's concern.
sentences.zh: 这引起了听众的关注。

sentences.en: And my brother yelled at me, God damn it, can't you even say hello?
sentences.zh: 我哥哥对我大喊，该死，你连你好都不会说吗？

sentences.en: I believe stuttering is trying to avoid stuttering.
sentences.zh: 我相信口吃是在试图避免口吃。

sentences.en: And I can remember asking one of the therapists we saw when my daughter became depressed, finding out that her boyfriend, that she was not his only girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 我记得当我女儿变得抑郁时，我问过我们看过的其中一位治疗师，发现她的男朋友，她不是他唯一的女朋友。

sentences.en: And we entered family therapy.
sentences.zh: 我们开始了家庭治疗。

sentences.en: And I asked the therapist, how can I help my son through his phase stuttering?
sentences.zh: 我问治疗师，我该如何帮助我儿子度过他的口吃阶段？

sentences.en: And he said, don't focus on it.
sentences.zh: 他说，不要关注它。

sentences.en: He's not stuttering.
sentences.zh: 他没有口吃。

sentences.en: He's just talking as well as he can.
sentences.zh: 他只是在尽他所能地说话。

sentences.en: And so are you.
sentences.zh: 你也是。

sentences.en: So I found the courage to enter speech therapy because I am a stutterer.
sentences.zh: 所以我找到了勇气去进行言语治疗，因为我是一个口吃者。

sentences.en: And when I was asked to give a talk in this room, I turned it down because, quote, I'm a stutterer, unquote.
sentences.zh: 当被要求在这个房间里演讲时，我拒绝了，因为，引用一下，“我是一个口吃者”。

sentences.en: But then I found the courage several days later to call her back and say, I'd like to do the talk.
sentences.zh: 但几天后，我找到了勇气回电说，我想做这个演讲。

sentences.en: And I am very proud to say that I found the courage to enter speech therapy, too, and get to my present level of fluency.
sentences.zh: 我很自豪地说，我也找到了勇气去进行言语治疗，并达到了我目前的流利水平。

sentences.en: It is stuttering is an interesting kind of extended metaphor.
sentences.zh: 口吃是一种有趣的扩展隐喻。

sentences.en: I've worked with a couple of people that have that.
sentences.zh: 我和几个有这种情况的人一起工作过。

sentences.en: And it seems like there's this intense energy to need to say something and be heard.
sentences.zh: 似乎有一种强烈的能量需要说出什么并被听到。

sentences.en: And also this fear of saying something and being heard and getting it wrong and getting in trouble.
sentences.zh: 同时也有一种害怕说出什么并被听到，然后弄错并惹上麻烦的恐惧。

sentences.en: Well said.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: I like that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: And they're bumping up against each other at the same time.
sentences.zh: 它们同时在相互碰撞。

sentences.en: So, you know, the speech stopped, you know, two conflicting energies.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，谈话停止了，你知道，两种相互冲突的能量。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think it's interesting, you know, that you have talked kind of about the parental energy, you know, throughout your life and all the things that you bring,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我觉得很有趣，你知道，你谈到了你一生中那种父母的能量，以及你所带来的一切，

sentences.en: that you kind of culminate with you writing this book.
sentences.zh: 最终促成了你写这本书。

sentences.en: Do you have anything to say about the book?
sentences.zh: 关于这本书，你有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: We have it in the Taproot waiting room.
sentences.zh: 我们在Taproot的候诊室里有这本书。

sentences.en: A lot of people have read it.
sentences.zh: 很多人都读过它。

sentences.en: And it's on Amazon, I'm proud to say.
sentences.zh: 我很自豪地说，它在亚马逊上有售。

sentences.en: Is It Okay to Cry by Winschaps, and it's about a dog?
sentences.zh: 书名是《可以哭吗？》（Is It Okay to Cry），作者是Winschaps，讲的是一只狗的故事？

sentences.en: I don't want to spoil the book, but do you have anything that you want to say?
sentences.zh: 我不想剧透，但你有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: It's about a puppy who's afraid to cry when his mother dies because he remembers that his father was called him a crybaby.
sentences.zh: 它讲的是一只小狗，在母亲去世时不敢哭，因为它记得父亲曾叫它“爱哭鬼”。

sentences.en: And it's the journey of the puppy whether he can find the courage to cry at his mother's funeral because he knows that his father dog will be there at his mother's funeral.
sentences.zh: 这是关于这只小狗的旅程，看它是否能鼓起勇气在母亲的葬礼上哭泣，因为它知道它的狗爸爸也会出现在葬礼上。

sentences.en: And one of the things in the book I would like to read, as a matter of fact, says,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想读一下书中的一段话，上面写着：

sentences.en: At age 11, Winn was orphaned, and at his mother's funeral was told by a family member that his mom wouldn't want him to cry.
sentences.zh: 11岁时，Winn成了孤儿，在母亲的葬礼上，一位家庭成员告诉他，他妈妈不会希望他哭的。

sentences.en: Thus, this book, and ultimately his career, helping folks know that owning and sharing their feelings is an important part of loving oneself.
sentences.zh: 因此，这本书，以及他最终的职业生涯，都是为了帮助人们认识到，承认并分享自己的感受是爱自己重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And, emphasis on the word and, loving yourself is a huge part of overcoming psychopathology.
sentences.zh: 而且，重点是“而且”，爱自己是克服心理病理学的关键部分。

sentences.en: Well, that's a beautiful, Winn.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那太美好了，Winn。

sentences.en: Do you have anything else that you want to, like, plug or say?
sentences.zh: 你还有什么想要宣传或说的吗？

sentences.en: The book is available on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 这本书在亚马逊上有售。

sentences.en: It isn't okay to cry by Winschaps.
sentences.zh: 书名是《可以哭吗？》，作者是Winschaps。

sentences.en: If you're a taproot patient, you can also check it out in our waiting room.
sentences.zh: 如果你是Taproot的患者，也可以在我们的候诊室里查看。

sentences.en: Is there anything else you'd like to say or encourage people to look up?
sentences.zh: 还有什么你想说或鼓励大家去了解的吗？

sentences.en: Have the courage to enter therapy if you feel the need to find someone with whom you feel safe.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得需要找一个让你感到安全的人，请鼓起勇气去接受心理治疗。

sentences.en: If you can tell anything, who can help you identify the psychogenesis, psychiatric origin of the issue you are facing.
sentences.zh: 如果你能说出任何事情，谁能帮你找出你所面临问题的心理起源。

sentences.en: Because, as a child, you learned what was and wasn't okay.
sentences.zh: 因为，作为孩子，你学会了什么是可以做的，什么是不可以做的。

sentences.en: And you learned there was no other place to live.
sentences.zh: 而且你学会了没有其他地方可以去。

sentences.en: Therefore, you should probably conform to what mom and dad say.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可能应该顺从父母所说的话。

sentences.en: Isn't it funny that Christians raise Christian children?
sentences.zh: 基督徒抚养基督徒的孩子，这不是很滑稽吗？

sentences.en: Mormons raise Mormon children.
sentences.zh: 摩门教徒抚养摩门教徒的孩子。

sentences.en: Jews raise Jewish children.
sentences.zh: 犹太人抚养犹太人的孩子。

sentences.en: And isn't it wonderful to know that it's okay to be you, even though I am proud to have gone to West Point.
sentences.zh: 知道做你自己是可以的，这难道不美妙吗？尽管我很自豪我曾就读于西点军校。

sentences.en: That it was okay to live my script practicing psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 能够按照我的剧本去实践心理治疗是可以的。

sentences.en: So, please, don't be afraid to see a therapist or a priest or a counselor in terms of overcoming scripts you may have learned.
sentences.zh: 所以，请不要害怕去看治疗师、牧师或咨询师，以克服你可能已经习得的剧本。

sentences.en: Girls shouldn't get angry.
sentences.zh: 女孩不应该生气。

sentences.en: Boys shouldn't cry.
sentences.zh: 男孩不应该哭。

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I'm working with a client who was ordered to strangle a puppy to death with her mother's gun sitting in the middle of the bed.
sentences.zh: 我正在辅导一位客户，她曾被命令用她母亲放在床中间的枪勒死一只小狗。

sentences.en: Which mom did every time they would sit down and talk.
sentences.zh: 每次她们坐下来谈话时，妈妈都会这样做。

sentences.en: And therapy is helping her know that it's okay to be soft.
sentences.zh: 心理治疗正在帮助她认识到，变得柔软是可以的。

sentences.en: You don't have to show power in order to be okay.
sentences.zh: 你不需要为了表现得好而展示力量。

sentences.en: So, I still practice because I love practicing therapy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我仍然在执业，因为我热爱心理治疗。

sentences.en: And may I always will.
sentences.zh: 愿我永远如此。

sentences.en: Well, it's beautiful, Lynn.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很美，Lynn。

sentences.en: Thank you for sitting down with us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你抽出时间与我们交谈。

sentences.en: And please check out Lynn's book.
sentences.zh: 请大家去看看Lynn的书。

sentences.en: And this is the Taproot Therapy PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是Taproot心理治疗播客。

sentences.en: We'll have a link to the book in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我们会在节目说明中提供这本书的链接。

sentences.en: And also on a blog post on GetTherapyBurningHim.com if anyone wants to pick that up.
sentences.zh: 如果有人想买的话，GetTherapyBurningHim.com的博客文章里也有链接。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for listening today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家今天的收听。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
